\chapter{Compactness}
\label{chap:compactness}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Compactness permits finite local data to control a global construction.
\begin{definition}
\label{def:compactness}
The space $X$ is compact if every open cover of $X$ has a finite subcover.\index{compactness}
\end{definition}
\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:compact-image}
If $X$ is compact and $f\colon X\to Y$ is continuous, then $f(X)$ is compact.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be an open cover of $f(X)$ in its subspace topology. The sets $f^{-1}(U_i)$ are open in $X$ and cover $X$. By \cref{def:compactness}, finitely many of these inverse images cover $X$. The corresponding sets $U_i$ cover $f(X)$.
\end{proof}
